channel.title: The Dig — Calibration, tuning and drift
channel.description: Papers relevant to operating, benchmarking, integrating and using a semiconductor spin-qubit quantum computer of at least 16 qubits that is co-located with and integrated into an HPC system. Today's arXiv announcement, ranked against the Calibration, tuning and drift preset. Today’s ranked reading list is led by 2611.30931, a must-read on calibration-insensitive spin-qubit pulses that sustain 99.97% fidelity and stable rotation angles over ten days in Si/SiGe, directly targeting drift and recalibration. The remaining skims span adjacent practical concerns: 2611.32388 offers shallow-circuit thermal-state preparation ideas transferable mainly through depth reduction; 2611.30508 and 2611.32560 provide low-resource QAOA constructions and application heuristics relevant to small noisy spin-qubit benchmarks; 2611.29983 presents a calibration-aware compilation and backend stack but lacks spin-qubit and HPC evidence; and 2611.31514 frames DOE-scale HPC-quantum integration strategy without concrete spin-qubit control or middleware methods. 1 must read.

item.title: Mitigating drift in spin-qubit control with calibration-insensitive pulses
item.description:
Must read new result — BIR-4 adiabatic pulses maintain 99% Clifford fidelity over a factor-of-2 drive power change and preserve rotation angle within 0.3° over ten days without recalibration. Calibrated composite CORPSE pulses reach 99.97% fidelity per gate and hold 99% Clifford fidelity over a ±0.9 MHz frequency offset.

Grade 0.484 · 3.1σ above the day's baseline · matched “Physical qubit calibration on a directed acyclic graph”

Figure

Rotation angle error and gate infidelities tracked across 53 gate-set tomography sessions over ten days without recalibration. BIR-4 suppresses rotation angle drift, even across an abrupt 1.3 MHz frequency jump, while square pulses drift continuously.

Asks

Can adiabatic and composite pulses mitigate the need for frequent recalibration of spin-qubit control parameters in silicon quantum dots?

Before

Standard square pulses require recalibration every few hours because drift in resonance and Rabi frequencies degrades control fidelity.

But

Single-qubit operations only. Longer pulse durations (CORPSE is ~4–8 times and BIR-4 is 16–32 times longer than square pulses) increase exposure to stochastic dephasing noise, setting a Markovian dephasing floor.

Tools

Si/SiGe double quantum dot with cobalt micromagnet · electric-dipole spin resonance · BIR-4 adiabatic pulse family · CORPSE composite pulse sequence · gate-set tomography

Abstract

Silicon spin qubits offer fault-tolerant control fidelities in a platform that is compatible with commercial foundries, but device calibration drifts and control parameters must be retuned every few hours. Here, we replace conventional square control pulses with two drift-resilient pulse families: the adiabatic BIR-4 and the composite CORPSE. In a Si/SiGe quantum-dot device, we benchmark single-qubit gate sets built from each pulse against deliberate miscalibration. We find that BIR-4 offers a 99% Clifford fidelity over a factor of 2 change in drive power and CORPSE maintains similar fidelity over +/-0.9MHz of offset. When fully calibrated CORPSE offers a 99.97% fidelity per gate, on par with a calibrated square pulse. Starting with tuned pulses, we then track errors using gate-set tomography for ten days without recalibration. BIR-4 holds its rotation angle to 0.3 degrees throughout, including across a 1.3MHz frequency jump. Our results demonstrate that these pulses can maintain high-fidelity operations without constant recalibration, mitigating the need for constant tuning, which is a key bottleneck in scaling quantum-dot-based quantum processors.

arxave:action.title: Prototype BIR-4/CORPSE on the 16-qubit spin QPU

item.arxave:action: Replace conventional square single-qubit pulses with BIR-4 and CORPSE on a subset of qubits, then run repeated 1Q randomized benchmarking and gate-set tomography over several days to measure how much the recalibration cadence can be relaxed.

arxave:action.title: Add drift-resilient pulse templates to the pulse-level API

item.arxave:action: Implement BIR-4 and CORPSE envelope generators with safe amplitude/frequency bounds, calibration metadata, and export hooks so they can be scheduled through the existing pulse-level API and queried alongside calibration state.

arxave:action.title: Ask authors about two-qubit and multi-qubit scaling

item.arxave:action: Ask whether the BIR-4/CORPSE drift resilience has been tested for two-qubit gates, crosstalk between neighboring dots, or simultaneous drive on many qubits, and how they would represent the pulse calibration state in an automated calibration database.

The paper reports one Si/SiGe device and single-qubit gates only; it does not establish 16-qubit addressability, two-qubit fidelity, readout fidelity, or HPC integration, so the team should treat it as a promising calibration method rather than a turnkey machine-level result.
